Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:

  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

# Continual-ARC task-e0d54f2b notes

## Rule
The input is divided into rectangular panels by full-color separator rows and columns. In each panel, count cells of the non-background marker color. Produce a compact output grid with one output cell per panel, preserving panel layout:
- output `1` if the panel contains exactly two marker cells;
- otherwise output the panel's background color.

Separators are not part of the panels. Determine the background/marker colors from the input (demo: background 4, marker 8; test: background 3, marker 2).

## Evidence
Demo 1 input was 23x8, split into 4x3 panels of 5x2 by zero separators. Output was 4x3 of 4s except bottom-right `1`. That panel alone contained exactly two 8s; all other panels had 0 or 1. Test input was 11x15, split into 4x4 panels of 2x3 by separator rows/columns of 8. Correct output (verified) was:
```
1 3 3 3
1 3 1 1
1 3 1 3
1 3 3 3
```
Those `1`s correspond exactly to panels with two 2s; all remaining output cells are background `3`.

## Caution
Do not infer output positions from marker coordinates within a panel; only count marker cells. A previous submitted grid incorrectly marked some panels; recount each panel carefully. This instance was solved after one wrong submission, so the rule has direct demo and test confirmation.
